doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Rock era, electric piano, move east
title: Leaving Las Vegas and finding the Nadelman house in Riverdale
summary: Driving east in 1961-62, house hunting in New York, and finding a cottage on the former Elie Nadelman estate.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And then the bossa nova came in hot and heavy and we left Las Vegas in 1961. We were there four years, bought a house, the whole thing. Sold the house in 1962 to the people we were renting it to, but we drove from Las Vegas with our little trailer behind the station wagon, with mops and brooms and buckets and kitchen stuff, and all of our Indian rugs, and just loaded up this trailer.
And left everything else in the house.
Left everything there, all the furniture.
And the kids, don’t forget the kids.

Oh yeah, count ‘em. And we drove to New York and stopped at a friend’s place, Don Payne, a bass player who worked with us and recorded with us, and we found a place to stay. We get into New York but the only place we could find somewhere was a motel and so in September, putting the kids in school in Riverdale, NY, and we’re making sandwiches in the motel for the kids, and taking them to school and then bringing them back, and looking for an apartment. Finally we looked and looked and looked and looked and nothing appealed to us because everything was like — here’s another cell in the beehive, on the 16th floor of this one. Here’s this apartment. I didn’t like any of them. I
saw an ad in the paper that said: old house, 5 acres of grounds, private drive, view of the river, and Jackie said, “let’s go look at it.” I said, oh, you know, “it’s going to be an arm and a leg.”

Forget it. The funny thing was on the way to New York I had said to Roy gee wouldn’t it be great if we could find an old house to live in, because we’d been living in this cement block kingdom in Vegas you know.

And I said to Jackie, that’s impossible. Angelic guidance took us to this place and so finally she talked me into looking at it. She says well let’s just look at it. So here we look at this house, there’s a driveway, it’s in a wonderful, private section called Alderbrook, with stone pillars to enter. I says oh this is going to be like four thousand dollars a month or something.
Right off the Henry Hudson River.
And you could look down and see the boats going by and it was right next to Dodge estate, and we found later that Robert Morgenthal, who is now State’s Attorney, lived right next door.
And just as important, the house used to belong to Elie Nadelman who is a very famous sculptor, and he’s in all the collections, you know, the Museum of Modern Art and the Rockefeller Collection.

Anyway we looked at it. And it was an 1880’s, 1865 house. Old. Real Victorian, all the doo dads up on the roof and everything. We looked at the place and there were about one, two, three, maybe five, six rooms.
This was just part of the house. It was a 21 room house. But there was a caretaker living in the main part of the house, and this part was being rented out.

Either it was guest quarters or servant’s quarters originally. Well we looked at it and there was wonderful things like a gas fireplace in the living room, a real fireplace in the bedroom, and we said gee this is wonderful, how much? Three hundred dollars a month. And at the time — wait a minute — at the time I wasn’t paying that much of a mortgage on the house, and I said oh that’s much too much, that’s ridiculous. And the bass player, who was with us, nudged me and he said, “if you don’t take it, I’m going to take it.”
Yeah. We were worried about the heat you know, like is it going to be heated, it’s such an old house. Is the plumbing going to work? That kind of thing.

So we had to wait ten days while the legal part of it, the lawyers had to check us out, check our kids out, go back through our backgrounds to give us the okay. And finally we got the okay and we moved in. We stayed there 11 years. And it was wonderful because up on the third floor, which we finally gained access to, were some of these Nadelman marble busts. We held them in our hands and looked at them. Wooden, marble, everything.
